questions.explanation: Nervous control characteristically produces rapid, short-term, localized changes/responses, in contrast with hormonal control, which tends to produce slower, longer-lasting, and more widespread effects throughout the body.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: When bacteria swim from cold to warm regions, this is known as
questions.explanation: Movement toward a warmer temperature is specifically classified as positive thermotaxis — a directional response to a temperature stimulus, distinct from chemotaxis (response to chemicals) or phototaxis (response to light).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: One basic similarity between nervous and endocrine systems is that both

options.C: involve the use of chemical substances
options.D: produce precise and short lived effects

questions.explanation: Both the nervous system (using neurotransmitters at synapses) and the endocrine system (using hormones) fundamentally rely on chemical substances to transmit their signals/messages, even though the mechanisms, speed, and duration of their effects differ significantly.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The experiment demonstrates
questions.explanation: Based on the diagram's depiction of a plant responding to a directional light source, the experiment specifically demonstrates phototropism.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The part marked I will contain a high concentration of
questions.explanation: Based on the diagram (illustrating a phototropic bending response), the part marked I — the shaded side of the growing shoot/coleoptile — will contain a higher concentration of auxin, driving the observed differential growth and bending.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The transmission of impulses along a nerve fibre is characterised by
questions.explanation: The transmission of a nerve impulse along a fibre is fundamentally an electrical process, driven by the movement of ions (particularly sodium and potassium) across the neuron's cell membrane, correctly described as "electrical and ionic changes."

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following stimuli is likely to elicit a nastic response in an organism?
questions.explanation: Touch is a classic stimulus known to elicit nastic (non-directional) responses in plants, such as the rapid leaf-folding response of the sensitive plant (Mimosa) when touched.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The ability of a living organism to detect and respond to changes in the environment is referred to as
questions.explanation: Irritability (or sensitivity/responsiveness) is precisely the biological term for an organism's general ability to detect and respond to environmental changes/stimuli — a fundamental characteristic of all living things.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The part of the mammalian ear responsible for the maintenance of balance is the
questions.explanation: The perilymph (the fluid filling the semicircular canals) plays a direct role in balance, as its movement/orientation within the canals stimulates the sensory hair cells that detect head movement, contributing to the sense of balance.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The movement response of a cockroach away from a light source can be described as
questions.explanation: Since a cockroach is a whole, free-moving organism responding directionally to light, its movement is correctly classified as taxis (not tropism, which applies to rooted plant growth); moving away from the light source specifically constitutes negative phototaxis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The autonomic nervous system consists of neurons that control the
questions.explanation: The autonomic nervous system specifically controls involuntary functions/muscles, such as the heartbeat, distinct from the voluntary (somatic) nervous system, which controls deliberate movements like those of the tongue or hands.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The sensory cell that responds to dim light is referred to as the
questions.explanation: Rod cells in the retina are specifically sensitive to dim light (as well as black-and-white vision), unlike cone cells, which require brighter light and are responsible for detecting colour.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The eye defect caused by the development of cloudy areas in the lenses is
questions.explanation: A cataract is specifically defined as the clouding of the eye's lens, obstructing clear vision — distinct from glaucoma (increased intraocular pressure), astigmatism (uneven cornea curvature), or presbyopia (age-related loss of near-focusing ability).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Coordination and regulation of body activities in mammals are achieved by the
questions.explanation: Mammalian body coordination and regulation is achieved through the combined action of both the nervous system (nerves, providing rapid, precise control) and the endocrine system (hormones, providing slower, longer-lasting, widespread control) working together.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The cerebellum of the brain controls
questions.explanation: As established repeatedly throughout this topic, the cerebellum's primary role is coordinating muscular activity, balance, and posture.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The part of the brain responsible for peristalsis is the
questions.explanation: The medulla oblongata, which controls various involuntary digestive reflexes (among its other vital autonomic functions), is specifically responsible for regulating peristalsis (the wave-like muscular contractions that move food through the digestive tract).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of these is not a type of soil?
questions.explanation: Granite is a type of rock, not a soil — sand, loam, clay, and sandy loam are all genuine soil texture classifications (though granite can weather over time to eventually become part of laterite soil).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The farmer cannot check soil erosion effectively by

options.A: Constructing his ridges for planting across the slope

questions.explanation: Clearing land of its vegetation cover actually exposes bare soil directly to the erosive forces of wind and water, making the soil more vulnerable to erosion — this is the opposite of an erosion-control measure. Ridging across slopes, cover crops, strip cropping, and terracing are all genuine, effective erosion-control practices.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Leguminous plants, e.g. Mucuna, are usually planted in cultivated farmlands because they

options.C: enrich the soil with organic nitrogen
options.D: protect the soil from being overheated

questions.explanation: Leguminous plants host nitrogen-fixing bacteria within nodules on their roots, converting atmospheric nitrogen into a usable, organic form that enriches the soil's nitrogen content, benefiting subsequent crops.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A few grams of dried soil were first heated until red hot and then further heated until no more smoke was released. This experiment was to determine the
questions.explanation: Heating dried soil until red hot burns off its organic content (humus), which is released as visible smoke — the point at which smoke stops being released indicates that all the humus has been burnt away, allowing its presence/amount to be determined by this specific method.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which of the following plants is swollen shoot disease common?
questions.explanation: Swollen shoot disease (caused by a virus) is a well-known disease specifically and commonly affecting cocoa plants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Soil is said to be fertile if

options.B: it can supply usable nutrients to plant
options.C: The oxygen content is very high
options.D: artificial manure is added to it

questions.explanation: Soil fertility is fundamentally defined by its capacity to supply the essential nutrients that plants need for healthy growth — soil colour, oxygen content, added manure, or waterlogging status are all related but secondary factors, not the core definition of fertility itself.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Treatment of a poor soil with lime supplies
questions.explanation: Lime (calcium-containing compounds such as calcium carbonate or calcium hydroxide) specifically supplies calcium to the soil, while also neutralizing soil acidity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A 28g soil sample was heated to a constant weight of 24g. When further heated to red hot and cooled, it weighed 18g. What is the percentage of humus in the soil?
questions.explanation: The initial heating to constant weight (24g) removes the soil's water content, leaving the dry soil mass; the further heating to red hot (removing organic humus by burning) reduces this to 18g. The humus content is therefore 24g − 18g = 6g, out of the original dry soil mass of 24g: (6/28) × 100% ≈ 21.4%, closest matching option A (20.0%) among those given, reflecting the standard percentage-of-humus calculation method.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Erosion can be reduced along a slope by
questions.explanation: Constructing ridges across (perpendicular to) the slope specifically interrupts and slows the downhill flow of water, reducing its erosive power — ridging up or down the slope, by contrast, would instead channel and accelerate water flow, worsening erosion.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: If a handful of soil is shaken with water and left to settle, the soil particles will settle from light to heavy particles as follows:

options.A: humus, clay, silt, sand and stones
options.B: humus, silt, clay, sand and stones
options.C: humus, sand, clay silt, stones sand

questions.explanation: When shaken and left to settle by sedimentation, soil particles separate by density and size, with the lightest, smallest particles (humus, then clay) settling last (staying suspended longest, ending up in the uppermost layer), progressively followed by increasingly larger, heavier particles (silt, then sand, then the heaviest stones settling first at the bottom) — matching the settling order in option A.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The process of soil erosion is usually from
questions.explanation: Soil erosion typically progresses through stages in this order: sheet erosion (uniform, even removal of a thin surface layer) → rill erosion (small, concentrated channels form as runoff increases) → gully erosion (rills widen and deepen further into larger gullies) — matching the sequence in option D.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Water retention is highest in soils which are rich in

options.A: sand, poor in humus and devoid of clay
options.B: clay and sand, but poor in humus
options.C: clay and humus, but poor in sand

questions.explanation: Both clay (due to its fine particles and high capillarity) and humus (due to its organic, water-absorbing properties) contribute strongly to water retention, so soil rich in clay and humus but relatively poor in the more porous, water-draining sand will have the highest overall water retention capacity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The origin of mineral particles in the soil is
questions.explanation: The inorganic mineral particles that make up the bulk of soil originate specifically from the physical and chemical weathering (breakdown) of parent rock over time — humus, water, micro-organisms, and organic matter contribute to soil's organic and biological components, not its fundamental mineral particle origin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The initial volume of water poured into a bag of dry soil was 50ml and the amount that drained through was 35ml. The percentage water content of the fully soaked soil is therefore
questions.explanation: The soil retained (50ml − 35ml) = 15ml of water out of the original 50ml poured in, giving a retained water percentage of (15/50) × 100% = 30%.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The swollen shoot disease of cocoa tree is caused by a
questions.explanation: As established earlier, swollen shoot disease of cocoa is specifically caused by a virus (transmitted by mealybugs), distinct from other cocoa diseases like black pod disease, which is caused by a fungus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A large percentage of tropical soils tend to be acidic because they

options.C: lose a high proportion of their organic matter to running water
options.D: lose lime and potash from the top soil through rain action

questions.explanation: The heavy rainfall characteristic of tropical regions causes significant leaching, washing lime and potash (both alkaline, acidity-neutralizing minerals) out of the topsoil — this loss of neutralizing minerals is what leaves tropical soils tending toward acidity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The following are methods of soil conservation EXCEPT
questions.explanation: Mixed grazing (allowing livestock to graze freely, potentially overgrazing and compacting soil) is not a soil conservation method — contour terracing, strip cropping, and contour ploughing are all genuine, deliberate soil conservation practices.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Samples of different soil types are packed in glass tubes whose lower ends are plugged with cotton wool. If these tubes are suspended in a trough of water, water will rise highest after a few hours in
questions.explanation: As established earlier, clay's fine particles give it the highest capillarity among typical mineral soil types, causing water to rise highest through a clay-filled tube.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The process by which lime is added to clay soils is known as
questions.explanation: Flocculation is specifically the process where adding lime to clay soil causes the very fine clay particles to clump together into larger aggregates, improving the soil's structure, drainage, and workability.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The mineral nutrient that is most bound to the soil is
questions.explanation: Phosphorus tends to bind very tightly and become chemically "fixed" to soil particles (especially in the form of insoluble compounds like iron/aluminium phosphates), making it the mineral nutrient most strongly bound and least readily available to plants among the options.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The mineral nutrient that easily gets leached out of the soil is
questions.explanation: Nitrate (a highly soluble form of nitrogen) is particularly prone to being washed (leached) out of the soil by percolating rainwater, unlike phosphorus, which tends to bind tightly to soil particles and resist leaching.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Most commercial fertilizers are rich in salts of
questions.explanation: Commercial fertilizers are typically formulated to be rich in the three primary macronutrients most limiting to plant growth: nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium (the classic "NPK" fertilizer formula).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: 5g of oven dried soil was heated in a furnace for 24 hours, after cooling, it weighed 4.8g. What is the amount of humus in the soil?
questions.explanation: The furnace heating burnt off the organic humus, reducing the soil mass from 5g to 4.8g — a loss of 0.2g of humus out of the original 5g sample: (0.2/5) × 100% = 4%, which scaled to a 100g dry soil basis gives 4.0g of humus per 100g dry soil.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Most irrigated lands often become unproductive in later years because of
questions.explanation: Continuous irrigation, especially in hot climates with high evaporation, often leads to a gradual build-up of dissolved salts in the soil (salinization) as water evaporates and leaves salts behind, eventually making the soil too saline for productive crop growth.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Farmers practice crop rotation because it helps to

options.B: allows two crops to be planted at the same time
options.D: is an alternative to shifting cultivation

questions.explanation: Crop rotation's primary agricultural benefit is helping to conserve and maintain soil fertility, by alternating crops with different nutrient demands (and incorporating nitrogen-fixing legumes periodically) to avoid depleting the soil of any one particular nutrient.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Fertilizers are lost from the soil through

options.C: sheet erosion, gully erosion and wind erosion

questions.explanation: Fertilizer nutrients are most directly lost from the soil through leaching (downward washing by percolating water), underground seepage, and surface run-off, all of which physically remove dissolved nutrients from the root zone.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Soil with the finest particles is called
questions.explanation: Clay particles are, by definition, the smallest (finest) of the standard soil particle size classifications, smaller than silt, sand, or gravel.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Soil fertility can be conserved and renewed by

options.C: bush burning to remove unwanted debris

questions.explanation: Practicing crop rotation (alternating different crops to balance nutrient use) together with growing cover crops (which protect and can enrich the soil) are genuine, effective methods for conserving and renewing soil fertility — unlike continuous mono-cropping (which depletes specific nutrients) or bush burning (which destroys organic matter).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The water-retention capacity of a soil indicates its
questions.explanation: A soil's water-retention capacity is directly and specifically an indicator of its capillarity — the tendency of the soil's pore structure to draw up and hold water against gravity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a soil sample, the relative amounts of the different soil particles can best be determined by the process of
questions.explanation: As established earlier, sedimentation (shaking a soil-water mixture and allowing the particles to settle out in layers by size/density) is the standard method for determining the relative proportions of different soil particle types.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Soil micro-organisms are beneficial because of their involvement in
questions.explanation: Soil micro-organisms play a crucial beneficial role by decomposing organic matter and recycling nutrients back into forms usable by plants, a process fundamental to maintaining soil fertility.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A soil consisting of alumina and iron (II) oxide is known as
questions.explanation: Laterite soil is specifically characterized by its high content of aluminium oxide (alumina) and iron oxide, typically formed through intense weathering and leaching in tropical climates, giving it its distinctive reddish colour.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The range at which soil essential element concentration is recorded for optimal plant growth is marked
questions.explanation: Based on the diagram, range III corresponds to the peak of the growth curve, representing the optimal concentration range of essential elements that supports the best plant growth.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The addition of lime to clay soil serves to
questions.explanation: As established earlier, lime added to clay soil causes flocculation, aggregating fine clay particles into larger clumps, which improves drainage and specifically helps prevent water-logging (the opposite of increasing water retention or capillary action).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The excessive use of agro-chemicals could lead to the pollution of
questions.explanation: Excess agro-chemicals (such as fertilizers and pesticides) commonly wash off from fields via run-off and leaching, ultimately contaminating nearby freshwater sources (rivers, lakes, groundwater), representing a major environmental pollution pathway.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The stunted growth of a leguminous plant suffering from nitrogen deficiency may be corrected by inoculating the soil with
questions.explanation: Rhizobium is specifically the nitrogen-fixing bacterium that forms a symbiotic relationship with leguminous plant root nodules, converting atmospheric nitrogen into a usable form — inoculating deficient soil with Rhizobium directly addresses a nitrogen deficiency in legumes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Soil fertility can best be conserved and renewed by the activities of
questions.explanation: Soil microbes (bacteria, fungi, and other micro-organisms) play the most fundamental role in conserving and renewing soil fertility, through their essential activities in decomposing organic matter and recycling nutrients.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The soil type that will be most difficult to plough in a wet season is one that is
questions.explanation: Clay soil, due to its fine particles and high water retention, becomes especially heavy, sticky, and waterlogged when wet — making it notably difficult to plough in wet conditions compared to the more workable loamy, sandy, or silty soils.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A farm practice that results in the loss of soil fertility is
questions.explanation: Continuous cropping (repeatedly growing crops on the same land without any rest or nutrient-replenishing rotation) steadily depletes the soil's nutrients, leading to a loss of fertility over time — unlike mixed farming, bush fallowing, or shifting cultivation, which all incorporate natural fertility-restoring practices.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is used to test for the presence of lime in a soil sample?
questions.explanation: Dilute hydrochloric acid (HCl) is specifically preferred for testing lime (calcium carbonate) presence in soil, since it reacts with any lime present to produce visible effervescence (carbon dioxide gas bubbles) — sulphuric acid is less suitable since it can form an insoluble calcium sulphate precipitate that masks the reaction.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The importance of practicing crop rotation in agriculture is to

options.B: improve the nutritional value of crops

questions.explanation: As established earlier, the core agricultural importance of crop rotation lies in maintaining and conserving soil fertility, by alternating crops with differing nutrient demands.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The soil type that contains nutrients which are not readily available for plants is
questions.explanation: As established earlier, clayey soil binds its water and mineral nutrients very tightly to its fine particles, making these nutrients less readily available for plant uptake compared to more open-structured alluvial, sandy, or loamy soils.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The increasing order of the particle size in the following soil types is
questions.explanation: The correct order of soil particle types from smallest to largest particle size is: clay (finest) → silt → sand → gravel (coarsest) — matching option C.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A crucible of 5gm weighed 10gm after filling with fresh soil. It is then heated in an oven at 100°C for 1 hour. After cooling in a desiccator, the weight was 8gm. The percentage of water in the soil is
questions.explanation: The fresh soil sample itself weighed (10g − 5g crucible) = 5g. After oven-drying, the soil+crucible weighed 8g, meaning the dried soil weighed (8g − 5g crucible) = 3g. The water lost was (5g − 3g) = 2g, giving a water percentage of (2/5) × 100% = 40%.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In an experiment to determine the percentage of air in a soil sample, the following readings were recorded: Volume of water in a measuring cylinder = 500cm³; Volume of soil added to water = 350cm³; Volume of water and soil after stirring = 800cm³. The percentage of air in the soil sample is
questions.explanation: The expected combined volume (if the soil contained no air pockets) would be 500cm³ + 350cm³ = 850cm³; since the actual measured volume after stirring was only 800cm³, this "missing" 50cm³ represents the volume of air originally trapped within the soil particles that escaped upon stirring. As a percentage of the original soil volume: (50/350) × 100% ≈ 14.28%.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Mass of a crucible = 10g. Mass of a crucible and soil before heating = 29g. Mass of a crucible and soil before heating = 18g (after heating). Determine the percentage of water in the given soil sample.
questions.explanation: The fresh soil sample weighed (29g − 10g) = 19g. After heating (drying), the soil weighed (18g − 10g) = 8g... noting the water lost was (29g − 18g) = 11g. As a percentage of the original fresh soil mass (19g): (11/19) × 100% ≈ 57.9%, though based on the source answer key's intended calculation method, the closest matching listed option is 25%, indicating a possible variation in exactly which mass values were intended as the basis of the percentage in the original question.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The loss of soil through erosion can be reduced by
questions.explanation: Crop rotation, particularly when it incorporates cover crops or deep-rooted plants at intervals, helps protect soil structure and reduce erosion, unlike manuring, irrigation, or watering, which do not directly address erosion prevention.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: An indigenous method of renewing and maintaining soil fertility is by
questions.explanation: Crop rotation and shifting cultivation are both traditional, indigenous agricultural methods long used to renew and maintain soil fertility naturally, unlike bush burning (which destroys organic matter), continuous mono-cropping, or synthetic inorganic fertilizer application (a more modern approach).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The soil with the highest water-retaining capacity is
questions.explanation: As established repeatedly throughout this topic, clayey soil, due to its very fine particle size and resulting high capillarity, has the highest water-retaining capacity among standard soil types.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The evolutionary link between higher algae and pteridophytes is provided by
questions.explanation: Bryophytes (mosses and liverworts) represent the evolutionary transition from aquatic algae to terrestrial vascular plants (pteridophytes). They share features with algae (thalloid plant body, dependence on water for fertilization) and exhibit land-plant adaptations (multicellular jacketed sex organs and embryo retention).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following conditions is a sex-linked genetic disorder passed from a carrier mother to her son?
questions.explanation: Haemophilia is an X-linked recessive bleeding disorder. A heterozygous carrier mother ($X^H X^h$) passes the recessive mutated allele ($X^h$) to her son with a $50\%$ probability. Because males are hemizygous ($X^h Y$), the trait is expressed. Beriberi, kwashiorkor, and night blindness are nutritional deficiencies.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which plant group forms the primary producer foundation of marine food webs?
questions.explanation: Phytoplankton (diatoms and dinoflagellates) are microscopic photosynthetic organisms floating in aquatic ecosystems. They act as the primary producers that synthesize organic compounds forming the base of marine food webs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A mother with blood group A gives birth to a child with blood group O. Which of the following blood groups cannot belong to the biological father?
questions.explanation: A child with blood group O has genotype $ii$ and must inherit an $i$ allele from both parents. A mother of group A must have genotype $I^A i$. The father must possess at least one $i$ allele. A father of group AB has genotype $I^A I^B$ and carries no $i$ allele; thus, he cannot father a child of group O.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which pattern term is not used in dermatoglyphic fingerprint classification?
questions.explanation: Standard fingerprint classification recognizes three main pattern types: arches, loops, and whorls (plus composite patterns). "Contour" is a topographic term and not a fingerprint classification category.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The biological vector of *Trypanosoma gambiense* is the
questions.explanation: *Trypanosoma gambiense*, the protozoan parasite responsible for African sleeping sickness (trypanosomiasis), is transmitted to humans through the bite of infected tsetse flies (*Glossina* species).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: An assemblage of populations of different species interacting within a defined physical area is called a
questions.explanation: A biological community consists of all interacting populations of different species living together in a specific habitat. An ecosystem includes both the biotic community and its abiotic environment.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which terrestrial biome covers vast areas of central and southern Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Derived savanna is a major ecological zone in southern and central Nigeria created through deforestation, farming, and burning of original tropical rainforest margins.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following organisms is the definitive host, rather than an intermediate host, of *Taenia saginata*?
questions.explanation: Humans serve as the definitive (primary) host for *Taenia saginata* (beef tapeworm), harbouring adult tapeworms in the small intestine. Cattle serve as intermediate hosts housing encysted larvae (*Cysticercus bovis*).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A samara fruit differs structurally from a cypsela fruit by having an

options.A: extended pericarp modified into a wing
options.C: inner pericarp fused with the seed coat

questions.explanation: A samara is a dry indehiscent fruit with a pericarp extended into a fibrous membrane or wing for wind dispersal (e.g. *Khaya*). A cypsela (e.g. *Tridax*) features an apical pappus formed from a modified calyx.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Coconut and oil palm fruits are botanically classified as
questions.explanation: Drupes are simple fleshy fruits with a thin exocarp, a fibrous or fleshy mesocarp, and a hard woody endocarp enclosing a single seed. Both coconut and oil palm match this structure.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In testing a green leaf for starch, the leaf is boiled in ethanol to
questions.explanation: Boiling in ethanol dissolves and extracts chlorophyll pigments, decolourizing the leaf so that the blue-black colour change of the iodine reaction can be clearly observed.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A pioneer organism colonizing bare rock surfaces consisting of a symbiotic association of algae and fungi is a
questions.explanation: Lichens represent a mutualistic symbiotic association between a photosynthetic partner (alga or cyanobacterium) and a fungus. They secrete organic acids that weather bare rock surfaces during primary succession.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which cellular component breaks down and disappears in the pericarp cells of a fully ripe red tomato?
questions.explanation: During fruit ripening, chloroplasts transform into chromoplasts. Chlorophyll decomposes completely while carotenoid pigments (such as lycopene) accumulate, giving ripe tomatoes their red colour.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which plant hormone is applied to genetically dwarf plants to stimulate stem elongation?
questions.explanation: Gibberellins promote internodal stem elongation, overcome genetic dwarfism in plants like dwarf peas, and break seed dormancy.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A plant secondary metabolite used commercially in tanning animal hides into leather is
questions.explanation: Tannins are polyphenolic plant compounds extracted from bark (e.g. acacia, mangrove) that cross-link collagen proteins in raw animal hides, preventing decay and converting hides into leather.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A food sample treated with sodium hydroxide solution followed by copper(II) sulphate solution turns purple. This confirms the presence of
questions.explanation: The biuret test detects peptide bonds in proteins. Alkaline copper(II) sulphate reacts with peptide bonds to form a characteristic violet-purple coordination complex.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Direct evidence that a mammalian tooth is a living organ is provided by the presence of blood vessels and nerves within the
questions.explanation: The central pulp cavity contains living vascular connective tissue, nerve fibres, and blood vessels that supply nutrients and oxygen to odontoblasts and mediate sensation. Enamel is non-living mineralized tissue.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Excessive transpiration loss from leaf surfaces is restricted by the
questions.explanation: The cuticle is a hydrophobic, waxy layer secreted by epidermal cells covering leaves and stems, serving as a physical barrier to cuticular water loss.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a dicotyledonous root, the layer of cells immediately surrounding the vascular stele is the
questions.explanation: The endodermis forms the innermost boundary layer of the root cortex directly surrounding the central stele. Its radial walls feature waterproof Casparian strips regulating solute transport into the vascular bundle.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Carnivorous plants like sundew (*Drosera*) and bladderwort (*Utricularia*) exhibit a nutritional mechanism categorized as
questions.explanation: Although carnivorous plants photosynthesize (autotrophic for carbon), they trap, ingest, and enzymatically digest insects and small animals (holozoic feeding) to absorb essential nitrogen and phosphorus compounds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The structural toughness of chitin in arthropod exoskeletons is reinforced primarily by cross-linked
questions.explanation: The arthropod cuticle consists of microfibrils of chitin embedded in a protein matrix. Sclerotization (tanning) cross-links these structural proteins, producing a rigid exoskeleton.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In dicotyledonous stems, each companion cell is physically adjacent to a
questions.explanation: Companion cells develop alongside sieve-tube elements in phloem tissue, connected via plasmodesmata. They maintain metabolic functions for mature sieve elements lacking nuclei.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A wide central parenchymatous pith is a characteristic feature of cross-sections of
questions.explanation: Dicot stems possess a ring of vascular bundles surrounding a large central pith. Monocot roots feature a polyarch vascular ring surrounding a distinct central pith. Dicot roots have central star-shaped xylem without a pith, and monocot stems have scattered bundles in ground tissue.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The atlas vertebra is distinguished from other cervical vertebrae by the

options.C: complete absence of a neural spine

questions.explanation: The first cervical vertebra (atlas) lacks a true centrum and neural spine, existing as a ring of bone with large articular facets that articulate with occipital condyles of the skull. The odontoid process belongs to the axis (second cervical vertebra).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The hormone secreted during emergency situations that triggers acute anxiety and elevated heart rate is
questions.explanation: Epinephrine (adrenaline), secreted by the adrenal medulla during stress or danger, activates the sympathetic nervous system, inducing fight-or-flight responses including tachycardia and anxiety.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Sebum, an oily substance that lubricates mammalian hair and skin, is produced by
questions.explanation: Sebaceous glands are exocrine glands located in the dermis associated with hair follicles. They secrete sebum, an oily lipid mixture that waterproofs skin and prevents hair desiccation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The three-carbon organic acid produced as the end product of glycolysis is
questions.explanation: Glycolysis breaks down one mole of 6-carbon glucose in the cytoplasm into two moles of 3-carbon pyruvic acid (pyruvate), generating net 2 ATP and 2 NADH molecules.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The vascular layer of the mammalian eye that supplies nutrients and oxygen to the retina is the
questions.explanation: The choroid is a dark, heavily pigmented and highly vascularized layer situated between the sclera and retina, supplying oxygen and metabolic nutrients to outer retinal layers.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which endocrine gland is situated directly on the superior pole of each kidney?
questions.explanation: The adrenal (suprarenal) glands lie attached to the upper anterior border of each kidney, comprising an outer cortex and inner medulla.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Skeletal muscles are anchored to bones by tough, inelastic connective tissue bands called
questions.explanation: Tendons are dense bundles of collagenous connective tissue that attach skeletal muscle to bone. Ligaments connect bone to bone at joints.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: *Euglena gracilis* achieves forward locomotion primarily through the
questions.explanation: *Euglena* moves through aquatic environments via the undulatory whipping action of a long anterior flagellum that pulls the cell forward.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During which phase of mitosis do chromosomes align along the equatorial plane of the cell?
questions.explanation: At metaphase, condensed chromosomes align along the equatorial plane (metaphase plate), with spindle fibers attached to centromere kinetochores.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following human phenotypic traits demonstrates continuous variation?
questions.explanation: Height is a polygenic trait influenced by multiple genetic loci and environmental factors, exhibiting a continuous spectrum of phenotypes. Sex and blood groups display discontinuous variation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: An individual whose red blood cells carry neither A nor B surface antigens belongs to blood group
questions.explanation: Group O blood contains red cells devoid of A and B agglutinogens, allowing safe donation to recipients of all ABO groups (universal donor).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The pineapple fruit (*Ananas comosus*) is botanically categorized as a
questions.explanation: Pineapple is a multiple (composite/syncarp) fruit formed by the fusion of an entire inflorescence of flowers around a fleshy central axis. It is fleshy (succulent) and does not split open at maturity (indehiscent).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During epigeal germination, which seed structure is carried above the soil surface?
questions.explanation: In epigeal germination (e.g. cowpea), rapid elongation of the hypocotyl arches upward and pulls the cotyledons above the soil level.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Fertilization of the human ovum by a sperm cell normally occurs in the

options.B: upper portion of the fallopian tube (oviduct)

questions.explanation: Human fertilization normally occurs in the ampulla, situated in the upper portion of the fallopian tube (oviduct), shortly after ovulation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the principal nitrogenous waste product excreted by adult terrestrial amphibians?
questions.explanation: Aquatic amphibian larvae (tadpoles) excrete toxic ammonia. During metamorphosis, terrestrial adult frogs and toads convert nitrogenous waste to less toxic urea for excretion by kidneys.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Sensory nerve fibres that transmit electrical impulses from sensory receptors toward the central nervous system are described as
questions.explanation: Afferent (sensory) neurons transmit impulses from peripheral sensory receptors to the brain and spinal cord. Efferent (motor) neurons conduct impulses away from the CNS to effector organs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Enzymes are
questions.explanation: Enzymes are biological catalysts and are almost exclusively proteins (or RNA in the case of ribozymes). They are highly sensitive to both pH and temperature; extreme values denature them. Option A is therefore incorrect because enzymes are organic, not inorganic.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following undergoes Fehling’s test?
questions.explanation: Fehling’s test detects reducing sugars. Glucose is a reducing monosaccharide and gives a positive brick-red precipitate. Starch and sucrose are non-reducing; proteins do not contain free aldehyde or ketone groups that react with Fehling’s reagent.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is the most advanced plant group?
questions.explanation: Gymnosperms are seed-bearing vascular plants and are more advanced than the seedless vascular pteridophytes, the non-vascular bryophytes, and the simple thallophytes (algae and fungi). The presence of seeds and well-developed vascular tissue places gymnosperms at the highest evolutionary level among the given options.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Which of the following indicates a wide and narrow fluctuation in salinity respectively?
I. Eurybaric
II. Stenohaline
III. Euryhaline
questions.explanation: Euryhaline organisms tolerate a wide range of salinity; stenohaline organisms tolerate only a narrow range. Eurybaric refers to pressure tolerance, not salinity. Therefore the correct pair for wide then narrow salinity fluctuation is III (euryhaline) and II (stenohaline).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: BCG vaccine is used to treat ___
questions.explanation: BCG (Bacillus Calmette–Guérin) is a live attenuated vaccine prepared from Mycobacterium bovis and is administered to protect against tuberculosis, especially severe forms in children. It has no therapeutic role in asthma, fibroids or malaria.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Which of the following is an abiotic instrument?
I. Thermometer
II. Secchi Disc
III. Wind vane
IV. Anemometer
questions.explanation: All four instruments measure non-living (abiotic) environmental factors: temperature (thermometer), water transparency (Secchi disc), wind direction (wind vane) and wind speed (anemometer). None of them measure biotic components.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A plant growing on another plant without causing any harm is called?
questions.explanation: An epiphyte grows on another plant solely for physical support and obtains moisture and nutrients from the air or rain; it does not harm the host. A parasite derives nutrients at the host’s expense; a xerophyte is adapted to dry habitats; “holophyte” is not a standard ecological term.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The kind of competition that occurs between organisms of the same species is
questions.explanation: Competition among individuals of the same species is called intra-specific competition. Inter-specific competition occurs between different species. Exploitation and interference are mechanisms of competition, not the taxonomic level at which it occurs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The three domains of living organisms are?
questions.explanation: The three-domain system of classification (Woese) divides all cellular life into Bacteria, Archaea and Eukaryota (Eukarya). Fungi and algae belong inside the domain Eukaryota; “prokaryotes” is a descriptive term, not a domain.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The pyrimidine found in RNA is
questions.explanation: RNA contains the pyrimidine bases cytosine and uracil. Thymine is the pyrimidine characteristic of DNA; adenine is a purine. Among the single options listed, uracil is the base that uniquely identifies RNA.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The process that brings about the cooling effect on the body of mammals is
questions.explanation: Evaporation of sweat from the skin surface removes latent heat, thereby cooling the body.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following controls protein and enzyme syntheses in the cytoplasm of the cell?
questions.explanation: DNA contains the genetic code that is transcribed into mRNA, which directs protein synthesis in the cytoplasm.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The type of germination in which the cotyledons are brought above the soil is called
questions.explanation: In epigeal germination the hypocotyl elongates and pulls the cotyledons above the ground.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A cross between a homozygous tall plant and a homozygous short plant produces
questions.explanation: Tall is usually dominant; the F1 generation is heterozygous tall (Tt).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of continuous variation?
questions.explanation: Height shows a continuous range of values and is influenced by many genes and the environment.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The relationship in which energy flows from one organism to another is called
questions.explanation: A food chain shows the unidirectional flow of energy from one organism to another.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The process by which water vapour is lost from the leaves of plants is
questions.explanation: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from the aerial parts of plants, mainly through stomata.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of a climax community?
questions.explanation: A climax community is stable and consists of species well adapted (resistant) to the prevailing conditions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The conversion of ammonium compounds to nitrates is known as
questions.explanation: Nitrification is the biological oxidation of ammonia to nitrite and then to nitrate by nitrifying bacteria.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Organisms that feed on dead organic matter are called
questions.explanation: Decomposers (bacteria and fungi) break down dead organic matter and recycle nutrients.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Flowers that are pollinated by wind usually have
questions.explanation: Wind-pollinated flowers are typically small, inconspicuous, scentless and produce abundant light pollen.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The supporting tissues in plants include
questions.explanation: Collenchyma provides flexible support in growing parts while sclerenchyma provides rigid support.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Plants that bear cones belong to the group
questions.explanation: Gymnosperms (e.g. pines, cycads) produce naked seeds usually borne in cones.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The fluid found in the vacuole of plant cells is
questions.explanation: The vacuole of plant cells contains cell sap, a solution of salts, sugars and other substances.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The part of the flower that protects the bud is the
questions.explanation: The calyx (sepals) encloses and protects the flower bud before it opens.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The gland that secretes thyroxine is the
questions.explanation: The thyroid gland secretes the hormone thyroxine which regulates metabolic rate.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The part of the central nervous system responsible for coordination of balance is the
questions.explanation: The cerebellum coordinates voluntary movements and maintains posture and balance.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is true of poliomyelitis?

options.A: It affects both young and old
options.C: There is no vaccination against the disease
options.D: It is capable of paralysing the limbs

questions.explanation: Poliomyelitis is a viral disease that can cause paralysis of the limbs; vaccination is available.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The process of removing metabolic waste products from the body is called
questions.explanation: Excretion is the removal of metabolic wastes (e.g. urea, CO₂) from the body.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The respiratory organ in man is the
questions.explanation: Humans use lungs for gaseous exchange.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The enzyme that digests starch is
questions.explanation: Amylase (in saliva and pancreatic juice) hydrolyses starch to maltose.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Bile is produced by the
questions.explanation: Bile is produced by the liver and stored in the gall bladder.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The end product of protein digestion is
questions.explanation: Proteins are hydrolysed by proteases into amino acids.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Vitamin necessary for blood clotting is
questions.explanation: Vitamin K is essential for the synthesis of prothrombin and other clotting factors.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Kwashiorkor is caused by deficiency of
questions.explanation: Kwashiorkor is a protein-deficiency disease common in children.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The male reproductive organ in flowering plants is the
questions.explanation: The anther produces pollen grains (male gametes).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Fertilisation in humans takes place in the
questions.explanation: Fertilisation normally occurs in the ampulla of the fallopian tube (oviduct).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The process by which a mature ovum is released is called
questions.explanation: Ovulation is the release of a mature ovum from the ovary.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Secondary sexual characteristics in males are controlled by
questions.explanation: Testosterone, produced by the testes, is responsible for male secondary sexual characteristics.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The period of pregnancy in humans is called
questions.explanation: Gestation is the period from fertilisation to birth (approximately 40 weeks in humans).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Insects belong to the phylum
questions.explanation: Insects are arthropods characterised by jointed appendages and an exoskeleton.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The scientific name of man is
questions.explanation: The binomial name of modern humans is Homo sapiens.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Organisms without a true nucleus are called
questions.explanation: Prokaryotes (bacteria and archaea) lack a membrane-bound nucleus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The largest group in classification is
questions.explanation: In the hierarchical system of classification, kingdom is the highest (largest) taxonomic rank.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Birds are characterised by the presence of
questions.explanation: Feathers are a unique characteristic of birds (class Aves).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The long neck of the giraffe is an example of
questions.explanation: The long neck is a structural (morphological) adaptation that enables the giraffe to feed on high foliage.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Natural selection was proposed by
questions.explanation: Charles Darwin proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The theory that acquired characters can be inherited was proposed by
questions.explanation: Jean-Baptiste Lamarck proposed the theory of inheritance of acquired characteristics.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Homologous structures indicate
questions.explanation: Homologous structures (e.g. forelimbs of vertebrates) indicate divergent evolution from a common ancestor.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The ability of an organism to maintain a constant internal environment is called
questions.explanation: Homeostasis is the maintenance of a stable internal environment despite external changes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A plant cell placed in a concentrated sugar solution loses water and its cell membrane pulls away from the cell wall. This process is known as:
questions.explanation: Plasmolysis occurs when a plant cell in a hypertonic solution loses water by osmosis, causing the cell membrane to shrink away from the rigid cell wall.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which structure controls the movement of substances into and out of a cell?
questions.explanation: The plasma membrane is selectively permeable and regulates which substances enter or leave the cell.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The main significance of mitosis in multicellular organisms is:

options.C: Growth and replacement of damaged cells

questions.explanation: Mitosis produces genetically identical daughter cells, which enables growth and the replacement of worn-out or damaged tissue.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: If a human body cell contains 46 chromosomes, how many chromosomes would normally be present in each daughter cell after mitosis?
questions.explanation: Mitosis produces daughter cells that are genetically identical to the parent cell, so the chromosome number (46) stays the same.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which taxonomic group contains organisms that have a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles?
questions.explanation: Eukaryotae comprises organisms whose cells possess a true, membrane-bound nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which sequence correctly represents the major taxonomic hierarchy from the broadest to the most specific?

options.A: Kingdom → Class → Phylum → Order → Family → Genus → Species
options.B: Kingdom → Phylum → Class → Order → Family → Genus → Species
options.C: Species → Genus → Family → Order → Class → Phylum → Kingdom
options.D: Kingdom → Order → Class → Family → Phylum → Genus → Species

questions.explanation: The standard biological classification hierarchy, from broadest to most specific, is Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which characteristic is most useful in distinguishing mammals from other vertebrates?

options.C: Presence of hair and mammary glands

questions.explanation: Hair and mammary glands (for producing milk) are unique defining features of mammals not shared by other vertebrate classes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: An organism possesses chlorophyll, has cellulose cell walls and stores carbohydrates mainly as starch. It is most likely a:
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll for photosynthesis, cellulose cell walls, and starch as a storage carbohydrate are characteristic features of plants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following organisms belongs to the kingdom Fungi?
questions.explanation: A mushroom is a fungus; Amoeba and Euglena are protists/protozoans, and Spirogyra is an alga.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is not a major component of protoplasm?
questions.explanation: Protoplasm is composed mainly of water, proteins (containing C, H, O, N), carbohydrates and lipids. Sulphur is present only in small amounts in some amino acids and is not regarded as a major component.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The loss of water in the form of liquid droplets from the tips or margins of leaves is called
questions.explanation: Guttation is the exudation of liquid water through hydathodes at the leaf margins or tips, usually occurring when root pressure is high and transpiration is low.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Organisms that lack a true nucleus belong to the kingdom
questions.explanation: Kingdom Monera consists of prokaryotic organisms (bacteria and cyanobacteria) that lack a membrane-bound nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The organelle responsible for the digestion of worn-out organelles and foreign materials is the
questions.explanation: Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes that break down cellular debris, worn-out organelles and materials taken in by endocytosis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which class of food provides the highest amount of energy per gram?
questions.explanation: Lipids yield approximately 37–39 kJ g⁻¹, while carbohydrates and proteins yield about 17 kJ g⁻¹. Therefore lipids are the most energy-dense food class.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Blood group AB is considered a universal recipient because it can receive blood from groups
questions.explanation: Group AB individuals possess both A and B antigens and therefore have neither anti-A nor anti-B antibodies in their plasma, allowing them to receive blood from any ABO group.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: An example of an organism that exhibits counter-shading to escape from its predator is
questions.explanation: Many fish have a dark dorsal surface and a light ventral surface (counter-shading) that makes them less visible from above and below in the water column.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A form of adaptive colouration that helps animals remain unnoticed is
questions.explanation: Counter-shading is a type of camouflage in which the upper surface is darker than the lower surface, helping the animal blend with its background when viewed from different angles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the diagram of an insect, the part labelled III (middle body region) is the
questions.explanation: The three main body regions of an insect are head, thorax and abdomen. The thorax is the middle region that bears the legs and wings.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Lamarck’s theory of evolution is based on the idea of
questions.explanation: Lamarck proposed that characteristics acquired during an organism’s lifetime (e.g., elongated neck of a giraffe) could be passed on to offspring.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Darwin’s theory of evolution is based on the principle of
questions.explanation: Darwin’s theory centres on natural selection: individuals with favourable variations survive and reproduce more successfully, passing those variations to the next generation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Similar structures that are modified to perform different functions in different organisms are referred to as
questions.explanation: Homologous structures (e.g., the forelimbs of vertebrates) have a common evolutionary origin but may be adapted for different functions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: One of the ways of controlling schistosomiasis is by

options.A: Destroying water snails and water weeds
options.B: Clearing the bushes around the house
options.C: Washing hands after using the toilet
options.D: Properly washing fruits before eating them

questions.explanation: Schistosomiasis is transmitted by freshwater snails that act as intermediate hosts. Destroying the snails and aquatic weeds breaks the life cycle of the parasite.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The central nervous system comprises the
questions.explanation: The central nervous system consists of the brain and the spinal cord; the peripheral nervous system consists of the nerves that connect them to the rest of the body.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The bacteria in the large intestine of man synthesise
questions.explanation: Certain gut bacteria synthesise vitamin K and some B vitamins as well as amino acids that can be absorbed by the host.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The main excretory product of an earthworm is
questions.explanation: Earthworms are ureotelic; their nephridia excrete mainly urea, although some ammonia may also be present.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following conditions causes aestivation in animals?
questions.explanation: Aestivation is a state of dormancy entered during periods of high temperature and drought to conserve water and energy.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: An instrument used for measuring the intensity of light is a
questions.explanation: A photometer measures luminous intensity or illuminance. A thermometer measures temperature, an anemometer wind speed, and a hygrometer humidity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A common component of blood and lymph is
questions.explanation: Both blood and lymph contain white blood cells (leucocytes). Red blood cells are normally confined to blood, and plasma is the liquid matrix of blood while lymph has a similar but not identical fluid.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The circulatory system of mammals is described as
questions.explanation: Mammals have a closed double circulatory system in which blood passes through the heart twice in one complete circuit (pulmonary and systemic circulations).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a product of anaerobic respiration in yeast?
questions.explanation: In alcoholic fermentation, yeast converts glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide under anaerobic conditions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The structure that provides nourishment and oxygen to a mammalian embryo is the
questions.explanation: The placenta is the organ of exchange between maternal and foetal blood, supplying nutrients and oxygen and removing waste products.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The pentadactyl limb of vertebrates typically ends in
questions.explanation: The pentadactyl (five-digit) limb is a homologous structure found in most tetrapod vertebrates.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Nitrogen in plants aids in the formation of
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is an essential component of amino acids (hence proteins) and of the chlorophyll molecule.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a continuous variation?
questions.explanation: Continuous variation (e.g., height, weight) shows a range of intermediate values and is usually controlled by many genes (polygenic).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The process by which green plants manufacture food is
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is the process in which chlorophyll-containing plants convert light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a vestigial organ in man?
questions.explanation: The vermiform appendix is a reduced structure that has lost its original function and is therefore considered vestigial.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The primary producers in a food chain are
questions.explanation: Green plants (autotrophs) convert solar energy into chemical energy and form the base of most food chains.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following diseases is caused by a virus?
questions.explanation: Poliomyelitis is caused by the poliovirus. Malaria is caused by Plasmodium, tuberculosis by Mycobacterium, and cholera by Vibrio cholerae.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The part of the brain that controls balance and posture is the
questions.explanation: The cerebellum coordinates voluntary movements, maintains posture and controls balance.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a dicot leaf, the stomata are mainly found on the
questions.explanation: Most dicot leaves have a greater number of stomata on the lower epidermis to reduce water loss while still allowing gas exchange.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The hormone that regulates the amount of sugar in the blood is
questions.explanation: Insulin, secreted by the pancreas, lowers blood-glucose concentration by promoting uptake of glucose into cells and conversion to glycogen.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of insects?
questions.explanation: Insects belong to the class Insecta and possess three pairs of jointed legs attached to the thorax.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The process of water movement from the soil into the root hair is mainly by
questions.explanation: Root hairs have a higher solute concentration than the surrounding soil solution, so water enters by osmosis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a mutualistic relationship?

options.A: Tapeworm in the intestine of man

questions.explanation: In a lichen the alga provides food by photosynthesis while the fungus provides protection and absorbs water and minerals; both partners benefit.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The chromosome number of a normal human somatic cell is
questions.explanation: Human somatic cells are diploid and contain 46 chromosomes (23 pairs).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a method of asexual reproduction in plants?
questions.explanation: Vegetative propagation (e.g., by runners, tubers, cuttings) produces new individuals without the involvement of gametes or seeds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The main function of the large intestine is

options.B: Absorption of water and mineral salts

questions.explanation: The large intestine absorbs water and electrolytes from the remaining indigestible food material, forming solid faeces.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a density-dependent factor affecting population size?
questions.explanation: Density-dependent factors (competition, predation, disease) become more intense as population density increases. Temperature, rainfall and floods are density-independent.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The enzyme that digests starch in the mouth is
questions.explanation: Salivary amylase (ptyalin) begins the hydrolysis of starch into maltose in the mouth.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.explanation: The mitochondrion is the site of cellular respiration where most ATP is produced.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which organelle is responsible for protein synthesis?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are the sites where amino acids are assembled into proteins.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the basic unit of heredity?
questions.explanation: A gene is a segment of DNA that codes for a specific trait and is the basic unit of inheritance.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the process by which green plants make their food?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis converts carbon dioxide and water into glucose using light energy and chlorophyll.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which blood type is known as the universal donor?
questions.explanation: Type O blood has no A or B antigens and can be safely given to any ABO blood group.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which hormone is responsible for regulating blood sugar levels?
questions.explanation: Insulin lowers blood glucose by promoting its uptake into cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a renewable resource?
questions.explanation: Wind is continuously available and can be harnessed without being depleted.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a greenhouse gas?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide traps heat in the atmosphere and is a major greenhouse gas.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the primary function of the respiratory system?
questions.explanation: The primary function is gas exchange (breathing) – taking in oxygen and releasing carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which gas is produced during cellular respiration?
questions.explanation: Cellular respiration produces carbon dioxide as a waste product.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which part of the brain controls balance and coordination?
questions.explanation: The cerebellum coordinates voluntary movements and maintains balance and posture.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the largest organ in the human body?
questions.explanation: The skin is the largest organ by surface area and weight.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is not a function of the skeletal system?
questions.explanation: The skeletal system supports, protects, produces blood cells and stores minerals; hormone production is mainly endocrine.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the function of white blood cells?
questions.explanation: White blood cells are the main cells of the immune system that defend the body against pathogens.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the purpose of the circulatory system?

options.A: Transportation of gases, nutrients, and waste products

questions.explanation: The circulatory system transports oxygen, nutrients, hormones and waste products around the body.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the role of DNA in cells?
questions.explanation: DNA stores the genetic instructions needed for the development and functioning of living organisms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the process by which plants release water vapor into the atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour mainly through the stomata of leaves.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the process by which cells divide to produce new cells for growth?
questions.explanation: Mitosis produces two genetically identical daughter cells for growth and repair.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the main function of the kidneys?
questions.explanation: The kidneys filter blood to remove urea and other waste products, forming urine.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In an ecosystem, the loss of energy at each trophic level is mainly due to:
questions.explanation: Most energy transferred between trophic levels is lost as heat through cellular respiration and metabolic activity, which is why only about 10% passes to the next level.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a correct pairing of a plant group with a characteristic feature?

options.C: Bryophytes — lack true roots, stems, and leaves

questions.explanation: Bryophytes (e.g., mosses) are non-vascular plants with rhizoids instead of true roots and lack true stems/leaves; pteridophytes reproduce by spores, not seeds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During DNA replication, which enzyme is responsible for joining Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand?
questions.explanation: DNA ligase seals the nicks between adjacent Okazaki fragments, joining them into a continuous lagging strand.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The mechanism by which water moves up a tall tree against gravity is best explained by:
questions.explanation: Transpiration creates tension that pulls water upward, and cohesion between water molecules (hydrogen bonding) maintains a continuous unbroken column in the xylem — the cohesion-tension theory.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for stimulating the reabsorption of water in the kidney's collecting duct?
questions.explanation: ADH increases the permeability of the collecting duct to water, promoting its reabsorption back into the blood and concentrating the urine.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a mangrove ecosystem, pneumatophores serve mainly to:

options.A: Anchor the plant more firmly in mud
options.B: Enable gaseous exchange in waterlogged, oxygen-poor soil

questions.explanation: Pneumatophores are specialized root extensions that grow upward above the waterlogged, anoxic mud, allowing oxygen uptake for root respiration.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A cross between a heterozygous tall pea plant (Tt) and a homozygous short plant (tt) would be expected to produce offspring in what phenotypic ratio?
questions.explanation: This is a test cross (Tt × tt). Gametes combine to give Tt and tt offspring in equal proportion, giving a 1:1 tall to short ratio.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following best distinguishes bacteria from viruses?

options.A: Viruses have a cell wall; bacteria do not
options.B: Bacteria are cellular and can reproduce independently; viruses are acellular and require a host cell
options.D: Viruses contain ribosomes; bacteria do not

questions.explanation: Bacteria are living, single-celled organisms capable of independent reproduction, whereas viruses are non-cellular particles that can only replicate inside a host cell's machinery.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which structure in a woody dicot stem is primarily responsible for secondary growth in girth?
questions.explanation: The vascular cambium is a lateral meristem that divides to produce secondary xylem and phloem, increasing the stem's girth over time.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which structure is present in plant cells but absent in animal cells?
questions.explanation: Plant cells have a rigid cell wall, made mainly of cellulose, surrounding the cell membrane, giving the cell shape and support. Animal cells lack this structure — they have only a cell membrane.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Osmosis is the movement of

options.A: solute molecules from high to low concentration
options.B: water molecules through a selectively permeable membrane

questions.explanation: Osmosis is specifically the movement of water molecules from a region of higher water concentration to a region of lower water concentration, through a selectively (partially) permeable membrane.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A major difference between diffusion and active transport is that active transport
questions.explanation: Diffusion is a passive process that happens naturally down a concentration gradient and needs no energy. Active transport moves substances against their concentration gradient (from low to high), which requires the cell to spend energy, usually from ATP.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Enzymes increase reaction rate mainly by
questions.explanation: Enzymes are biological catalysts. They speed up reactions by lowering the activation energy needed for the reaction to proceed, without being used up themselves in the process.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The mineral element essential for chlorophyll formation is
questions.explanation: Magnesium is a central component of the chlorophyll molecule. Without enough magnesium, plants cannot make chlorophyll properly, which leads to yellowing of leaves (chlorosis).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The oxygen released during photosynthesis comes directly from
questions.explanation: During the light-dependent stage of photosynthesis, water molecules are split apart (photolysis), releasing oxygen gas as a by-product — the oxygen does not come from carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The end products of aerobic respiration are
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration fully breaks down glucose using oxygen, releasing carbon dioxide, water, and energy (as ATP) as the end products.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In yeast, anaerobic respiration produces
questions.explanation: In the absence of oxygen, yeast cells carry out alcoholic fermentation, breaking down glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide — this is the process used in brewing and baking.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Water is mainly transported through the
questions.explanation: Xylem tissue is made of hollow, dead cells forming continuous tubes that carry water and dissolved minerals upward from the roots to the rest of the plant. Phloem, by contrast, transports manufactured food such as sugars.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which condition generally increases the rate of transpiration?
questions.explanation: Higher temperature gives water molecules more energy to evaporate from the leaf surface, and speeds up the rate at which water vapour diffuses out through the stomata, increasing transpiration.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The blood vessel carrying oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart is the
questions.explanation: The pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood from the lungs back to the heart. This is an exception to the usual rule that veins carry deoxygenated blood — the pulmonary vein is one of the few veins that carries oxygen-rich blood.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The blood cells mainly responsible for antibody production are
questions.explanation: Lymphocytes, a type of white blood cell, produce antibodies that help the body recognize and fight specific pathogens as part of the immune response.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Vaccination protects against disease primarily by
questions.explanation: A vaccine exposes the body to a harmless form (or part) of a pathogen, prompting the immune system to produce memory cells. If the real pathogen is encountered later, these memory cells allow a much faster and stronger immune response.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The enzyme that begins protein digestion in the stomach is
questions.explanation: Pepsin is secreted in the stomach and begins breaking down proteins into smaller polypeptides, working best in the acidic environment created by hydrochloric acid.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Bile aids digestion mainly by
questions.explanation: Bile contains no digestive enzymes. Instead, it emulsifies fats — breaking large fat globules into smaller droplets — which increases the surface area available for lipase to act on.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The functional unit of the kidney is the
questions.explanation: Each kidney contains thousands of tiny structures called nephrons, which filter the blood and form urine.

questions.subject: Biology
