questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option that best completes the gap: Neither the teacher nor the students ____ present at the meeting.
questions.explanation: When subjects are joined by “neither \ldots nor”, the verb agrees with the nearer subject. “Students” is plural, so “were” is correct.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option that has a different stress pattern from the others.
questions.explanation: “Dedication” is stressed on the third syllable (de-di-CA-tion) while the others are stressed on the third syllable in a similar pattern, but the odd one out in many JAMB items is the one with a different primary stress placement; here dedication follows the common -tion pattern but is listed as the distinct item in the 2024 set.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word underlined: Accountants are discreet with their records.
questions.explanation: “Discreet” means careful and prudent in one’s speech or actions, especially in order to avoid causing offence or to gain an advantage; the closest meaning is “cautious”.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option that best completes the gap: The boy was advised to ____ from bad company.
questions.explanation: “Keep away from” is the correct phrasal verb meaning to avoid association with.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word underlined: The politician’s speech was full of ambiguity.
questions.explanation: “Ambiguity” means the quality of being open to more than one interpretation; lack of clarity. The opposite is “clarity”.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option that best completes the gap: If I ____ you, I would accept the offer.
questions.explanation: In hypothetical conditional sentences the subjunctive “were” is used for all persons: “If I were you \ldots”.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word underlined: The committee’s decision was irrevocable.
questions.explanation: “Irrevocable” means impossible to revoke or change; final and binding.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option that has the same vowel sound as the underlined letter(s) in “cough”.
questions.explanation: The vowel sound in “cough” is /ɒ/ as in “hot”.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option that best completes the gap: She is the ____ of the two sisters.
questions.explanation: When comparing two people the comparative form “taller” is required.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word underlined: The soldier showed great valour in battle.
questions.explanation: “Valour” means great courage in the face of danger. The opposite is “cowardice”.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option that best completes the gap: The teacher asked the students to ____ their assignment.
questions.explanation: “Hand in” means to submit work to a teacher or superior.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word underlined: The news of his promotion was received with alacrity.
questions.explanation: “Alacrity” means cheerful readiness or eagerness.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option that has a different consonant sound from the others.
questions.explanation: “Ink” ends with the velar nasal /ŋ/ followed by /k/, while the others end with the pure /ŋ/ sound; the distinct final sound makes it the odd one out.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option that best completes the gap: It is high time we ____ home.
questions.explanation: The expression “It is high time \ldots” is followed by the past tense (subjunctive) form: “went”.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word underlined: The weather was extremely harsh during the winter.
questions.explanation: “Harsh” in this context means severe or unpleasantly extreme. The opposite is “mild”.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word underlined: The speaker’s argument was fallacious.
questions.explanation: “Fallacious” means based on a mistaken belief; misleading or deceptive.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option that best completes the gap: Neither of the candidates ____ qualified for the post.
questions.explanation: “Neither” is singular and takes a singular verb: “is”.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option that has the correct stress: dedication
questions.explanation: The primary stress in “dedication” falls on the third syllable: de-di-CA-tion.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word underlined: The manager’s decision was arbitrary.
questions.explanation: “Arbitrary” means based on random choice or personal whim rather than any reason or system.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option that best completes the gap: The students were advised to ____ the instructions carefully.
questions.explanation: “Read through” means to examine or study carefully from beginning to end.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word underlined: The path was narrow and winding.
questions.explanation: “Narrow” means of small width. The opposite is “broad” (or wide).

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option that best completes the gap: She prefers tea ____ coffee.
questions.explanation: The correct preposition after “prefer” when comparing two things is “to”.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word underlined: The athlete’s performance was mediocre.
questions.explanation: “Mediocre” means of only average quality; not very good.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option that has a different vowel sound from the others.
questions.explanation: “Bout” has the diphthong /aʊ/, while the others contain the /ʊ/ sound.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option that best completes the gap: The committee has ____ a decision.
questions.explanation: “Come to a decision” is the correct collocation meaning to reach a conclusion.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word underlined: The story he told was fictitious.
questions.explanation: “Fictitious” means not real or true; invented. The opposite is “true”.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option that best completes the gap: Hardly had he arrived ____ it started raining.
questions.explanation: The correct correlative conjunction after “hardly \ldots” is “when”.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word underlined: The lawyer’s argument was cogent.
questions.explanation: “Cogent” means clear, logical and convincing.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Identify the correctly punctuated sentence.

options.D: "It is a beautiful day", she said

questions.explanation: "It's" is the correct contraction of "it is." The comma belongs inside the closing quotation mark before "she said."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Select the word nearest in meaning to "MERETRICIOUS."
questions.explanation: "Meretricious" describes something that is superficially or garishly attractive but actually has no real value.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Select the word opposite in meaning to "PARSIMONIOUS."
questions.explanation: "Parsimonious" means extremely unwilling to spend money; its opposite is "generous."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: "By the time the fire fighters arrived, the whole building _____ down."
questions.explanation: The past perfect tense ("had burnt") is used because the burning was completed before another past action (the fire fighters' arrival).

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which of the following sentences is in the passive voice?

options.B: The budget was approved by the committee.
options.C: The committee is approving the budget.
options.D: The committee will approve the budget.

questions.explanation: In passive voice, the subject receives the action. Here "the budget" (the object of the action) becomes the subject, with "was approved by" showing the passive construction.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Identify the correct rendering of the given stress pattern for the word "PHOTOGRAPHY."
questions.explanation: "Photography" is stressed as pho-TOG-ra-phy, with primary stress on the second syllable.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option that correctly identifies the type of clause underlined: "The man who stole the bicycle has been arrested."
questions.explanation: "Who stole the bicycle" describes/modifies the noun "the man," which is the function of a relative (adjectival) clause.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Select the option nearest in meaning to the idiom "to let the cat out of the bag."
questions.explanation: This idiom means to accidentally disclose a secret or piece of hidden information.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option with the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling has a double "c" and double "m": ACCOMMODATE.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which word is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to "defiled" as used in the passage?
questions.explanation: In the passage, "defiled" means spoiled, corrupted, or polluted by political interference. The opposite is "sanctified", which means made pure or kept sacred. "Forged" means faked, "degenerated" means declined, and "disparaged" means belittled.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: How has politics been related to educational institutions after independence?

options.A: Educational institutions received political support without political interference.
options.B: Educational institutions received neither political support nor political interference.
options.C: Educational institutions received political support at the cost of political interference.
options.D: Educational institutions experienced substantial political interference with little genuine political support.

questions.explanation: The passage explicitly states: "What we have actually received is infinite political interference with little genuine political support."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which word is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to "hamper" as used in the passage?
questions.explanation: "Hamper" means to hinder, obstruct, or impede ("hamper radical social transformation"). "Foster" means to encourage, promote, and support the growth of something, which is its direct antonym. "Accelerate" refers to speed rather than support versus obstruction.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word.
As the triumphant rebels were returning to their base, they met with a serious REVERSE.
questions.explanation: "Reverse" here means a sudden setback, defeat, or change from good fortune to bad. The contrast with "triumphant" confirms that they met with a defeat.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word.
I believe that extreme poverty can turn a lawyer into a PETTIFOGGER.

options.A: A low-class lawyer given to mean or dishonest dealings

questions.explanation: A pettifogger is an unscrupulous, petty lawyer who relies on trickery, dishonest methods, or trivial arguments.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined phrase.
If Joy had not been TRIPPED UP halfway through the race, she would have come first.
questions.explanation: To be "tripped up" in this context means to be obstructed, stumbled, or interrupted in progress. "Interrupted" captures the idea of being stopped midway.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word.
The director's remark was extremely APPOSITE to the issue being discussed.
questions.explanation: "Apposite" means highly relevant, suitable, or appropriate to the circumstances.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word.
Was there any PRESAGE before the unexpected incident?
questions.explanation: A "presage" is a sign, omen, or warning indicating a future event.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Fill in the gap with the correct option.
The attitude of my students to ________ baffles me.
questions.explanation: The correct noun spelling is "pronunciation" (with "-nun-", unlike the verb "pronounce").

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Fill in the gap with the correct option.
Dr. Josh saw Dr. Jeremiah ________ an egg against the wall.
questions.explanation: Verbs of perception (e.g. *see*, *watch*, *hear*) followed by an object take a bare infinitive (without *to*) to describe a completed action: "saw Dr. Jeremiah smash an egg".

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Fill in the gap with the correct option.
Toluwani ________ Dr. Jeremiah's notes since she came home.
questions.explanation: The preposition "since" followed by a specific past point ("since she came home") requires the present perfect continuous tense ("has been reading") to express an activity that started in the past and continues to the present.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Fill in the gap with the correct option.
Amina is an ________ of the University of Lagos.
questions.explanation: "Alumna" is the singular noun for a female former student. "Alumnus" is male singular, "alumni" is male/mixed plural, and "alumnae" is female plural.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Fill in the gap with the correct option.
Your academic performance will improve if you ________ hard.
questions.explanation: First conditional sentences use simple present tense in the *if*-clause ("if you practise") to refer to a real future possibility. "Practise" with an 's' is the verb form in British/Nigerian English.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option that MOST APPROPRIATELY completes the sentence.
The Lagos International Trade Fair ________ annually.
questions.explanation: Events are "held" (passive voice). Since "Lagos International Trade Fair" is a singular subject and "annually" indicates a regular habit, the simple present passive "is held" is required.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option that MOST APPROPRIATELY completes the sentence.
Sola ran ________.

options.A: round twice the town before supper
options.B: twice round town before the supper
options.C: round the town twice before supper
options.D: round the town before supper twice

questions.explanation: The natural word order for adverbs following a verb of movement is Place ("round the town"), Frequency ("twice"), and Time ("before supper").

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option that MOST APPROPRIATELY completes the sentence.
He promised to complete the assignment in no time. This means he would do the work ________.
questions.explanation: The idiom "in no time" means almost instantly or very quickly.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option that MOST APPROPRIATELY completes the sentence.
John's father has just bought a ________ car.
questions.explanation: Standard adjective ordering is: Age/Condition ("brand new") + Colour ("blue") + Origin ("Japanese") + Purpose/Type ("sports") + Noun ("car").

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option that MOST APPROPRIATELY completes the sentence.
The delegates were given ________.
questions.explanation: A compound numerical modifier preceding a noun takes a hyphen and a singular unit: "a two-hour break".

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option that MOST APPROPRIATELY completes the sentence.
Garba acquiesced ________ their decision despite his reservations.
questions.explanation: The verb "acquiesce" requires the preposition "in" ("acquiesce in something").

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option that MOST APPROPRIATELY completes the sentence.
Snakes and Ladders ________ me happy these days.
questions.explanation: "Snakes and Ladders" is the singular title of a single board game, taking a singular verb "makes". "These days" demands simple present tense.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option that MOST APPROPRIATELY completes the sentence.
The property of the jailed former local government chairman has been ________.
questions.explanation: Correct spelling is "confiscated" (c-o-n-f-i-s-c-a-t-e-d).

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option that MOST APPROPRIATELY completes the sentence.
I will deliver the goods next week ________.
questions.explanation: "Without fail" is a fixed idiomatic phrase meaning guaranteed or without exception.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option that MOST APPROPRIATELY completes the sentence.
The true greatness of a country is believed to ________ the well-being of its citizens.
questions.explanation: "Consist in" means to reside in or have as an essential quality. "Consist of" means composed of physical parts. "Comprise of" is grammatically incorrect.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option MOST NEARLY OPPOSITE in meaning to the underlined word.
The Senate President was criticized for being too COMPROMISING with the executive arm, and members wanted a leader who was far more rigid.
questions.explanation: "Compromising" means yielding, flexible, or ready to grant concessions. The antonym is "rigid" (unyielding, inflexible).

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option MOST NEARLY OPPOSITE in meaning to the underlined word.
The latest policy of the Central Bank has not ALLAYED public fears about inflation; rather, it has aggravated them.
questions.explanation: To "allay" fears means to reduce, calm, or alleviate them. The opposite is to "aggravate" (worsen or intensify) them.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option MOST NEARLY OPPOSITE in meaning to the underlined word.
Mr. Manu is difficult to convince because he is an OPINIONATED manager.
questions.explanation: "Opinionated" describes someone who holds narrow, dogmatic personal views. The opposite is "objective" (impartial, detached, relying on facts).

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option MOST NEARLY OPPOSITE in meaning to the underlined word.
From the outset of the trial, the boy was SANGUINE, whereas the girl was hopeless.
questions.explanation: "Sanguine" means optimistic, cheerful, and confident. The opposite is "hopeless" or pessimistic.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the most appropriate option for gap (31).
questions.explanation: A "discrepancy" is an unexpected difference or inconsistency between two things (pronunciation and spelling).

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the most appropriate option for gap (32).
questions.explanation: The preposition "by" is required: determining spelling "by its pronunciation" (using sound as a guide).

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the most appropriate option for gap (33).
questions.explanation: The text refers to the English "spelling system".

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the most appropriate option for gap (34).
questions.explanation: The context contrasts the literate upper classes with the common, illiterate population ("uneducated people").

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the most appropriate option for gap (35).
questions.explanation: The passage discusses the transition of English from a spoken tongue to a "written language".

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the most appropriate option for gap (36).
questions.explanation: Historical copyists and document writers are termed "scribes".

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the most appropriate option for gap (37).
questions.explanation: "Idiosyncrasies" refers to peculiar or unique structural habits (spelling peculiarities).

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the most appropriate option for gap (38).
questions.explanation: "Inserted" means placed or put inside a word.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the most appropriate option for gap (39).
questions.explanation: "Corresponding" means matching (the equivalent Latin word).

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the most appropriate option for gap (40).
questions.explanation: The central theme is how spoken "pronunciation" evolved while written spelling stayed static.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option that gives the MOST APPROPRIATE INTERPRETATION of the sentence.
The property is going under the hammer. This means the house is being ________.
questions.explanation: "Under the hammer" means sold at an auction sale.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option that gives the MOST APPROPRIATE INTERPRETATION of the sentence.
A Gilbertian situation means a ________.
questions.explanation: Derived from W.S. Gilbert, "Gilbertian" refers to a situation characterized by paradoxical, topsy-turvy, or humorously absurd circumstances.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option that gives the MOST APPROPRIATE INTERPRETATION of the sentence.
Students often patronize flea markets. This means they shop at ________.

options.A: markets where specialized equipment is sold
options.B: markets where fake goods are sold

questions.explanation: A "flea market" is an open-air market selling inexpensive, used, or second-hand goods.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option that gives the MOST APPROPRIATE INTERPRETATION of the sentence.
The opposition accused several politicians of engaging in shenanigans. This means they demonstrate ________.
questions.explanation: "Shenanigans" refers to secret, deceitful, or dishonest activities and trickery.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option that gives the MOST APPROPRIATE INTERPRETATION of the sentence.
In informal slang, referring to someone as a bit of crumpet implies the person is ________.
questions.explanation: In colloquial usage, "a bit of crumpet" refers to a person regarded as physically or sexually attractive.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option that gives the MOST APPROPRIATE INTERPRETATION of the sentence.
Mobutu is a dead ringer for Bagudu. This means Mobutu ________.

options.C: closely resembles Bagudu in physical appearance

questions.explanation: A "dead ringer" is an exact duplicate or close physical resemblance to another person.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option that gives the MOST APPROPRIATE INTERPRETATION of the sentence.
The lady excused herself to powder her nose. This means she ________.
questions.explanation: "Powder one's nose" is a polite euphemism for visiting the toilet/restroom.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option that gives the MOST APPROPRIATE INTERPRETATION of the sentence.
The journalist noted that the minister's comments were off the record. This means the comments were ________.

options.A: not written in government record books
options.B: not intended for public disclosure or publication

questions.explanation: "Off the record" means information provided confidentially, not meant to be published or quoted publicly.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option that gives the MOST APPROPRIATE INTERPRETATION of the sentence.
It was a collective project, but Samson tried to steal the show. This means Samson ________.

options.A: tried to rob the team of earnings
options.C: tried to draw all public attention and credit to himself

questions.explanation: To "steal the show" means to divert attention, praise, or credit from others to oneself.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option that gives the MOST APPROPRIATE INTERPRETATION of the sentence.
The soldier was wounded by friendly fire. This means he ________.

options.A: was attacked by an enemy posing as a friend
options.B: was injured in a brawl with a companion
options.C: was hit by weapons fired accidentally by his own military forces
options.D: was injured by an explosive device

questions.explanation: "Friendly fire" refers to accidental weapon fire coming from one's own military side.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option with the SAME VOWEL SOUND as the underlined sound in *s<u>ay</u>s*.
questions.explanation: *Says* is pronounced /sez/ with the short vowel sound /e/. *Said* is pronounced /sed/, sharing the exact same vowel sound /e/. Options A, B, and C contain the diphthong /eɪ/.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option with the SAME VOWEL SOUND as the underlined sound in *c<u>our</u>se*.
questions.explanation: *Course* is pronounced /kɔːs/ with the long vowel /ɔː/. *Coarse* is pronounced /kɔːs/ (a homophone). *Worse* and *curse* contain /ɜː/, while *cot* contains /ɒ/.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option with the SAME VOWEL SOUND as the underlined letter *i* in *favour<u>i</u>te*.
questions.explanation: The letter *i* in *favourite* (/ˈfeɪvərɪt/) represents the short vowel /ɪ/. *Kin* (/kɪn/) contains the same short vowel /ɪ/. *Fight* and *write* have /aɪ/, while *keen* has /iː/.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option that contains the consonant sound /l/.
questions.explanation: The /l/ sound is pronounced in *table* (/ˈteɪbl/). In *calm*, *would*, and *talk*, the letter 'l' is silent.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option that RHYMES with *coax*.
questions.explanation: *Coax* is pronounced /kəʊks/. *Chokes* is pronounced /tʃəʊks/, matching the ending sequence /-əʊks/.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the option that RHYMES with *brother*.
questions.explanation: *Brother* (/ˈbrʌðə/) rhymes directly with *mother* (/ˈmʌðə/), both ending in /-ʌðə/.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option with the CORRECT STRESS PATTERN.
egregious
questions.explanation: *Egregious* is pronounced /ɪˈɡriːdʒəs/, with primary stress on the second syllable (e-GRE-gious).

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the option with the CORRECT STRESS PATTERN.
cooperative
questions.explanation: *Cooperative* is pronounced /kəʊˈɒpərətɪv/, carrying primary stress on the second syllable (co-OP-er-a-tive).

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
The word in CAPITAL LETTERS carries emphatic stress. Select the question that elicits this response:
"My father READ the newspaper."

options.B: Did your father steal the newspaper?

questions.explanation: Emphatic stress on READ highlights the action performed, contrasting it with another action like stealing ("Did he steal it? No, he READ it").

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
The word in CAPITAL LETTERS carries emphatic stress. Select the question that elicits this response:
"The president SPOKE to the press."

options.A: Did the president speak to the press?
options.B: Did the president write to the press?
options.D: Are these the pressmen that the president spoke to?

questions.explanation: Emphatic stress on SPOKE highlights the medium of communication, contrasting speaking with writing.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The manager was reluctant to approve the proposal. The opposite of "reluctant" is:
questions.explanation: "Reluctant" means unwilling or hesitant; its direct opposite is "willing."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The student's explanation was plausible. This means that the explanation was:
questions.explanation: "Plausible" means seeming reasonable or probable, i.e. believable.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The witness gave a credible account of the incident. The opposite of "credible" is:
questions.explanation: "Credible" means believable or trustworthy; its opposite is "doubtful," meaning not easily believed.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Neither the principal nor the teachers ___ aware of the change in timetable.
questions.explanation: With "neither...nor," the verb agrees with the noun closer to it. Since "teachers" (plural) is nearer the verb, "were" is correct.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: If I ___ you, I would reconsider the decision.
questions.explanation: This is a hypothetical/subjunctive condition, which conventionally takes "were" regardless of subject: "If I were you..."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: By the time the doctor arrived, the patient ___ unconscious.
questions.explanation: The past perfect tense ("had become") is used for an action completed before another past action (the doctor's arrival).

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The committee recommended that the proposal ___ immediately.
questions.explanation: After verbs like "recommend" expressing a demand or suggestion, the subjunctive form ("be implemented") is used.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The quality of the products ___ improved considerably.
questions.explanation: The subject of the sentence is "the quality" (singular), not "products," so it takes the singular verb "has."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The students were prohibited ___ entering the laboratory without supervision.
questions.explanation: The correct idiomatic collocation is "prohibited from" doing something.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When the principal asked who had damaged the equipment, everyone kept mum. This means that everyone:
questions.explanation: The idiom "kept mum" means remained silent or said nothing.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The new student cut corners while carrying out the assignment. This means that the student:

options.C: used shortcuts, often at the expense of quality

questions.explanation: "Cut corners" is an idiom meaning to do something in the easiest or cheapest way, often sacrificing quality.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: If the statement is: "It is not beyond the realm of possibility that he will win." It means that:
questions.explanation: "Not beyond the realm of possibility" is a double negative meaning something is possible, so the correct reading is that he may possibly win.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: "Hardly had the examination begun when the power supply was interrupted." This means:

options.A: The examination ended before the power went off
options.B: The power went off shortly after the examination began
options.D: The power went off long before the examination

questions.explanation: "Hardly...when" indicates that one event (power interruption) followed almost immediately after another (the exam beginning).

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The witness's statement was inconsistent with the evidence. The word "inconsistent" means:
questions.explanation: "Inconsistent" means not in agreement or contradictory, i.e. not matching the evidence.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The doctor advised the patient to ___ smoking.
questions.explanation: The correct idiomatic preposition is "desist from," meaning to stop doing something.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Let us go for the lecture, ___?
questions.explanation: Sentences beginning with "Let us" (suggestions) take the question tag "shall we?"

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Nobody informed the students about the change, ___?
questions.explanation: "Nobody" is treated as negative, so the tag must be positive; informally, "they" is used to refer back to "nobody," giving "did they?"

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which of the following words is most associated with medicine?
questions.explanation: "Dosage" refers to the amount of a medicine to be taken, making it a medical term; the others relate to law and finance.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which of the following is most appropriate in the context of banking?
questions.explanation: "Overdraft" is a banking term referring to withdrawing more money than is available in an account.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Many Nigerians are yet to appreciate the importance of ______ good food.
questions.explanation: “Eating” is the most natural and commonly used collocation with “good food” in this context.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The major reason for this lack of ______ is to be found in the pattern of spending.
questions.explanation: The passage discusses lack of awareness of the importance of good food.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: This pattern is characterised by lack of ______.
questions.explanation: The wasteful spending habit points to lack of proper planning.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: A good number of whom are quite ______ when it comes to buying clothes.
questions.explanation: The context of spending heavily on expensive clothes shows they are extravagant.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: This ______ for expensive clothes has been brought about by the belief that it is appearance that ______.
questions.explanation: Desire for expensive clothes is linked to the belief that appearance produces the type of person one is.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The accident victims bled "PROFUSELY".
questions.explanation: Profusely means in large amounts / excessively.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Although our leader preached "EGALITARIANISM", he could not match it up with action.
questions.explanation: Egalitarianism means belief in equality of all people.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: My sister married a "DOTING" husband.
questions.explanation: Doting means extremely fond / loving.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Okolo played the piano with great "DEXTERITY".
questions.explanation: Dexterity means skill and neatness in using the hands.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: They have tried to "CIRCUMVENT" the restriction on the importation of the commodities.
questions.explanation: Circumvent means to find a way around / bypass a rule or restriction.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The chairman’s verdict "REDRESSED" the injustice meted out by the secretary.
questions.explanation: Redressed means corrected or put right; the opposite is aggravated (made worse).

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Sola could not travel yesterday because of the "SEVERITY" of the weather.
questions.explanation: Severity means harshness; the opposite is mildness.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: He devoted much time to the "PERIPHERAL" aspect of the topic.
questions.explanation: Peripheral means minor or of little importance; the opposite is main.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Laide is "IMMUNE" to the flattery of young men.
questions.explanation: Immune means not affected by; the opposite is susceptible (easily affected).

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The chairman advised every member of the group to tolerate "DISPARATE" dispositions.
questions.explanation: Disparate means different or contrasting; the opposite is converging (coming together / similar).

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Who is the protagonist of The Lekki Headmaster?
questions.explanation: Mr Adewale Adebepo, popularly called Bepo, is the central character and principal of Stardom Schools.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What major event opens the novel The Lekki Headmaster?

options.B: Mr Bepo breaking down in tears at morning assembly
options.C: The MD announcing a fee increase

questions.explanation: The novel begins with the usually confident principal unable to speak and weeping uncontrollably during assembly.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Why was Mr Bepo under intense pressure to leave Nigeria?

options.A: He had been dismissed from Stardom Schools
options.B: His wife Seri and children were already in the UK and wanted him to join them
options.C: He had received a better job offer from another school
options.D: He wanted to start a commercial transport business

questions.explanation: Bepo’s wife Seri (a nurse in the UK) and their daughters had already relocated and constantly pressured him to “japa”.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the central physical setting of The Lekki Headmaster?
questions.explanation: Almost the entire story unfolds at Stardom Schools located in the affluent Lekki area of Lagos.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What does the term “JAPA” primarily refer to in the novel?

options.B: The mass migration of Nigerians abroad in search of a better life

questions.explanation: “Japa” describes the contemporary Nigerian phenomenon of relocating abroad for better opportunities.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: How much was the boarding-house fee per session at Stardom before it was reduced?

options.A: One hundred and sixty-three thousand naira
options.B: Two hundred and fifty thousand naira
options.C: One hundred and sixty thousand naira

questions.explanation: The novel states that the boarding fee was reduced from ₦250,000 as part of the school’s fee-restructuring strategy.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: At the end of the novel, what decision does Mr Bepo finally take?

options.A: He boards the flight to the UK
options.B: He resigns and starts his own school immediately
options.C: He returns to Stardom Schools, declaring that his heart is in Nigeria
options.D: He accepts a transfer to another branch of the school

questions.explanation: After the grand farewell, Bepo surprisingly returns and announces that he is not going abroad; his heart and mission remain at Stardom.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Why was Mr Bepo nicknamed “The Lekki Headmaster”?

options.A: He lived in Lekki during his time as a headmaster
options.B: He humorously imitated characters from the classic TV drama Village Headmaster
options.C: He introduced a new curriculum in the school

questions.explanation: The nickname stuck because of his humorous imitation of characters from the popular Nigerian television series Village Headmaster while resolving conflicts.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What was Mr Bepo’s monthly salary at Stardom Schools?
questions.explanation: The novel states that Bepo’s monthly salary as principal was ₦400,000.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the main challenge that Mr Bepo faces in the novel?

options.A: Convincing parents to enrol their children
options.C: Balancing his career with pressure to migrate

questions.explanation: The central conflict is Bepo’s internal struggle between remaining committed to his students in Nigeria and the strong family pressure to relocate to the UK.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The principal turned a deaf ear to the students' complaints. This means that he
questions.explanation: To "turn a deaf ear" to something means to deliberately ignore it or refuse to listen to it — the principal chose not to pay attention to the complaints.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: If a politician sits on the fence, he

options.A: refuses to take a definite position

questions.explanation: Someone who "sits on the fence" avoids committing to either side of an issue — they refuse to take a clear, definite position.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The manager said that the new employee had a chip on his shoulder. This means the employee
questions.explanation: To have "a chip on one's shoulder" means to carry a lingering feeling of resentment or grievance, often over feeling unfairly treated — it describes someone who is unnecessarily resentful, not someone who is injured or generous.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The scientist's explanation left no stone unturned. This means that the scientist
questions.explanation: This idiom means to try every possible way or method to achieve something — it describes a very thorough effort, not carelessness.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The man's audacious behaviour shocked everyone.
questions.explanation: "Audacious" describes behaviour that is bold and daring, often in a way that surprises or shocks others.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The teacher was meticulous in marking the scripts.
questions.explanation: "Meticulous" describes someone who pays very careful, close attention to detail — being thorough rather than careless or quick.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The witness gave a plausible explanation.
questions.explanation: "Plausible" means something seems reasonable or likely to be true — in other words, believable.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The minister's speech was concise.
questions.explanation: "Concise" means expressing something clearly using few words — in other words, brief.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The student's answer was ambiguous.
questions.explanation: "Ambiguous" describes something that can be understood in more than one way, making its meaning unclear.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The government plans to curtail unnecessary expenditure.
questions.explanation: "Curtail" means to cut short or reduce something, especially spending, rights, or activities.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The man's benevolent actions were praised.
questions.explanation: "Benevolent" describes actions or a person that are kind, generous, and well-meaning — in other words, charitable.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The chairman's decision was arbitrary.
questions.explanation: "Arbitrary" means based on random choice or personal whim rather than any reason or system. Its opposite is "systematic," meaning done according to a fixed plan or method.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The witness gave a credible account.
questions.explanation: "Credible" means believable or trustworthy. Its opposite is "doubtful," which suggests something is uncertain or hard to believe.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The medicine had an adverse effect.
questions.explanation: "Adverse" means harmful or unfavourable. Its opposite is "beneficial," meaning helpful or advantageous.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: His argument was coherent.
questions.explanation: "Coherent" describes something that is logical, clear, and easy to follow. Its opposite is "confused," describing something disorganized or hard to understand.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The candidate was reluctant to accept the offer.
questions.explanation: "Reluctant" means unwilling or hesitant to do something. Its opposite is "eager," which means enthusiastic and willing.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Neither the students nor their teacher ______ aware of the change.
questions.explanation: With "neither...nor," the verb agrees with the nearer subject. The nearer subject here is "teacher," which is singular, so the verb must be singular: "was."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: By the time we arrived, the lecture ______.
questions.explanation: The lecture had already started before the group arrived, so the past perfect tense ("had begun") is needed to show that one past action happened before another past action.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The committee ______ divided in its opinion.
questions.explanation: "Committee" is a collective noun. Since the sentence uses the singular possessive "its," the committee is being treated as one single unit here, so it takes the singular verb "is."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: She prefers reading ______ watching television.
questions.explanation: The correct construction is "prefer something TO something else" (not "than"), so "to" is the correct word to complete this comparison.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: He has lived in Ibadan ______ 2022.
questions.explanation: "Since" is used with a specific point in time (like a year or date) to show when an ongoing action started. "For" would instead be used to state a duration, such as "for three years."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The students arrived ______ the examination had started.
questions.explanation: The examination had already begun (shown by the past perfect "had started") before the students arrived, so "after" correctly shows that their arrival happened later than the start of the exam.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: I would rather you ______ here tonight.
questions.explanation: After "would rather" when talking about someone else's action, English uses a past tense form even though the meaning is present or future — this subjunctive-like structure makes "stayed" the correct choice here.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: One of my friends ______ going to Lagos tomorrow.
questions.explanation: The subject of the sentence is "one" (singular), not "friends," so the verb must be singular: "is."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Hardly had the teacher entered ______ the students became silent.
questions.explanation: "Hardly...when" is a fixed idiomatic pairing used to show that one event happened immediately after another. It is not paired with "than," which instead pairs with "no sooner."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: No sooner had he arrived ______ it began to rain.
questions.explanation: "No sooner...than" is the fixed idiomatic pairing used to show that one event happened immediately after another.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The woman, together with her children, ______ arrived.
questions.explanation: The main subject of the sentence is "woman" (singular); the phrase "together with her children" is a parenthetical addition and does not change the number of the subject, so the verb stays singular: "has."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: In the sentence, "The boy ran quickly," the word "quickly" is a/an
questions.explanation: "Quickly" describes how the boy ran — it modifies the verb "ran" — which is exactly what an adverb does.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: In "The book on the table is mine," the expression "on the table" functions as
questions.explanation: "On the table" begins with the preposition "on," followed by its object "the table." A phrase built this way, starting with a preposition, is called a prepositional phrase.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which sentence is correctly punctuated?
questions.explanation: When "however" starts a sentence as a linking word meaning "nevertheless," it should be followed by a comma to separate it from the rest of the sentence.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which word is correctly spelt?
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is "privilege" — note there is no "d" before the "g," unlike the common misspelling "priviledge."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The quality of the products ______ excellent.
questions.explanation: The subject of the sentence is "quality" (singular), not "products," so the verb must be singular: "is."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Each of the boys ______ a book.
questions.explanation: "Each" is always treated as singular, even when followed by a plural phrase like "of the boys," so the verb must be singular: "has."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The police ______ investigating the matter.
questions.explanation: "Police" is one of a small group of nouns that are always treated as plural in standard English, so it takes the plural verb "are."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Mathematics ______ one of his favourite subjects.
questions.explanation: Although "Mathematics" ends in "-s," it refers to a single subject and is treated as a singular noun, so it takes the singular verb "is."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The pair of shoes ______ under the bed.
questions.explanation: The subject of the sentence is "pair," which is treated as a single unit here, so it takes the singular verb "is."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as "seat."
questions.explanation: "Seat" and "beat" both contain the long vowel sound /iː/. "Sit," "set," and "said" all have different, shorter vowel sounds.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as "cup."
questions.explanation: "Cup" and "luck" both contain the short vowel sound /ʌ/, as in "cut" or "much." The other options have different vowel sounds — "put" and "boot" have rounded vowel sounds, and "food" has a long /uː/ sound.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which word has a different vowel sound?
questions.explanation: "Beat," "seat," and "meat" all contain the vowel sound /iː/, but "great" is pronounced with /eɪ/ instead, making it the odd one out.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which word rhymes with "light"?
questions.explanation: "Light" is pronounced /laɪt/, and "height" is pronounced /haɪt/ — both share the same ending vowel and consonant sounds, which is what makes them rhyme.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which word has the same initial consonant sound as "chair"?
questions.explanation: "Chair" and "church" both begin with the /tʃ/ sound. "Chemist," "character," and "chorus" all begin with a /k/ sound instead, even though they're all spelled with "ch."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which word contains a silent "k"?
questions.explanation: In English, the letter "k" is silent when it comes before "n" at the start of a word, as in "knee," "knife," and "know." In "king," "keep," and "kind," the "k" is pronounced normally.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which word has the stress on the second syllable?
questions.explanation: "Relax" is stressed on its second syllable (re-LAX). "Table," "doctor," and "present" (as used here) are all stressed on their first syllable.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which word has the stress on the first syllable?
questions.explanation: "Teacher" is stressed on its first syllable (TEACH-er). "Begin," "about," and "allow" are all stressed on their second syllable instead.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which word has a different consonant sound for the underlined letter combination "ch"?
questions.explanation: "Ch" in "machine" is pronounced /ʃ/, unlike the /tʃ/ sound heard in "chair," "church," and "child."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which word contains the /θ/ sound?
questions.explanation: "Thin" contains the unvoiced "th" sound /θ/, as in "think" or "three." "Then," "this," and "those" all contain the voiced "th" sound /ð/ instead.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The expression "to spill the beans" means to
questions.explanation: "To spill the beans" means to reveal secret or private information, often accidentally or before it was meant to be known.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: If someone "hit the nail on the head," the person
questions.explanation: This idiom describes doing or saying something with complete accuracy, getting to the exact point of a matter — much like a hammer striking a nail precisely on its head.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The expression "once in a blue moon" means
questions.explanation: "Once in a blue moon" describes something that happens very rarely or almost never, since a "blue moon" — a second full moon in one calendar month — is itself an uncommon event.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The student's success was attributed to hard work. The expression means that his success was
questions.explanation: To say something is "attributed to" a cause means that cause is credited with being responsible for it — his success was said to be the result of his hard work.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The sentence "The manager had the report typed" means that

options.A: the manager typed the report personally
options.B: someone typed the report for the manager
options.D: the manager refused to type the report

questions.explanation: This is the causative structure "have + object + past participle." "Had the report typed" means the manager arranged for somebody else to type it, not that he typed it himself.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the difference between the approaches of Socrates and Aristotle?

options.A: Aristotle felt the need for repetition to develop good habits in students; Socrates felt that students need to be constantly questioned.
options.B: Aristotle felt the need for rote-learning; Socrates emphasized on dialogic learning
options.D: Aristotle emphasized on the importance of paying attention to human nature; Socrates emphasized upon science.

questions.explanation: The passage clearly contrasts Aristotle’s use of systematic teaching and repetition to form good habits with Socrates’ method of questioning listeners to draw out their own ideas. Option A captures this exact difference.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Why do educationists consider philosophy a “weak and woolly” field?

options.B: Its theoretical concepts are easily understood.
options.D: Its tenets are not educative enough.

questions.explanation: The passage states that many educationalists consider philosophy “a weak and woolly field, too far removed from the practical applications of the real world to be useful.” Hence it is seen as lacking practical application.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What were Plato’s beliefs about education?

options.A: He believed that only the rich have the right to acquire education.
options.B: He believed that education should be holistic.
options.C: He believed that only a select few are meant to attend schools.
options.D: He believed that not all pupils are talented.

questions.explanation: The passage states that Plato believed education should be holistic, including facts, skills, physical discipline, music and art.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Why did Aquinas propose a model of education which did not lay much emphasis on facts?

options.B: Facts do not lead to holistic education.
options.C: Facts change with the changing times.

questions.explanation: The passage explains that Perennialism (Aquinas) focuses on principles and reasoning rather than facts “which are apt to change over time.”

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Who is the protagonist and principal of Stardom Schools in The Lekki Headmaster?
questions.explanation: Mr Adewale Adebepo, popularly called Bepo or “The Lekki Headmaster”, is the central character and principal of Stardom Schools.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What was the common ritual at the morning assembly at Stardom on Tuesdays and Thursdays?

options.C: The second stanza of the national anthem

questions.explanation: On Tuesdays and Thursdays the school recited the second stanza of the national anthem as a regular assembly ritual.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The governor asked the corrupt official to leave the public service forthwith.
questions.explanation: “Forthwith” means at once / immediately.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The meeting was cancelled because of the protest.
questions.explanation: “Called off” is the standard phrasal verb meaning cancelled.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The word is stressed on the penultimate syllable.
questions.explanation: Penultimate = second to the last.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: He was simultaneously a director of cultural affairs and a visiting lecturer.
questions.explanation: “Simultaneously” means at the same time = contemporaneously.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The only impediment to the project is finance.
questions.explanation: Impediment = obstacle / hindrance.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: His remarks were pejorative.
questions.explanation: Pejorative means expressing contempt or disapproval = derogatory.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The ostensible reason for his resignation is lack of interest in the job, but it is beyond that.
questions.explanation: Ostensible = apparent / seeming (not necessarily the real reason).

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The sailor inadvertently killed the albatross.
questions.explanation: Inadvertently = unintentionally / accidentally.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: It was a deluge of blessing.
questions.explanation: Deluge literally means a great flood; figuratively an overwhelming quantity.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The student had to perform the herculean task of digging trenches as punishment of his offence.
questions.explanation: Herculean = requiring great strength or effort = arduous.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Habib: Do you mind if I sit down here? Umana: Well, yes I do actually.

options.A: Umana is reluctantly granting the request
options.B: Umana is willingly accepting the request
options.C: Umana is certainly rejecting the request
options.D: Umana is objecting to the request

questions.explanation: “Yes I do (mind)” is a clear refusal of the request.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The Governor held forth for several minutes on the need to fight corruption in the state.

options.A: The Governor was silent for minutes when corruption was being discussed.
options.B: The Governor whispered a few things about corruption.
options.C: The Governor spent time saying a few things about corruption.
options.D: The Governor gave a rather long speech on the need to fight corruption.

questions.explanation: “Held forth” means spoke at length / delivered a speech.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The boss is fond of throwing his weight about.

options.C: The boss gives orders to people
options.D: The boss is respected by his employees.

questions.explanation: “Throwing one’s weight about” means using one’s authority in an overbearing way / giving orders.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Ronaldo is the live wire of the team.

options.B: Ronaldo is the captain of the team.
options.C: Ronaldo is the most energetic in the team.

questions.explanation: A “live wire” is an energetic, lively person who animates the group.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: If I were in London I would have watched the game.

options.A: I did not watch the game although I was in London.
options.B: I was in London and I did not watch the game.
options.C: I did not watch the game so I hope to travel to London
options.D: I was not in London and I did not watch the game.

questions.explanation: The conditional “If I were… I would have…” indicates that the speaker was neither in London nor watched the game.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The student gave evasive answers to the questions being asked by her teacher.
questions.explanation: Evasive = avoiding the truth; opposite is direct.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The increase in transport fares deterred our school from planning an excursion this year.
questions.explanation: Deterred = discouraged / prevented; opposite is encouraged.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Abu is naturally taciturn.
questions.explanation: Taciturn = habitually silent; opposite is garrulous (talkative).

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The corpulent woman is his mother.
questions.explanation: Corpulent = fat / obese; opposite is slender.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: He describes his wife as pusillanimous.
questions.explanation: Pusillanimous = cowardly / lacking courage; opposite is brave.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Our ______ are the teenagers.
questions.explanation: The correct fixed expression is “target audience” (singular collective).

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Babajide deceived my father; Babajide is a ______.
questions.explanation: The person who deceives is a cheat (or cheater); “dupe” is the victim.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: He is an ______ liar.
questions.explanation: “Inveterate” means confirmed / habitual. (Note: option D is identical; in a real exam only one correct form appears. Correct spelling is inveterate.)

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The teacher told the students to ______ the girl for her brilliant performance.
questions.explanation: The standard collocation is “clap for” someone.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The man teaches in the university, so he is ______.
questions.explanation: A university teacher is an academic. “Academician” usually refers to a member of an academy.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The old man, with his wives, ______ guilty.
questions.explanation: The subject is “the old man” (singular); the phrase “with his wives” is parenthetical and does not change the verb.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The novel ______ twenty five chapters.
questions.explanation: “Comprises” does not take “of”. Correct: The novel comprises twenty-five chapters.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: He sold me a ______ radio.
questions.explanation: “Duff” means worthless / of poor quality (informal British English).

questions.subject: English
questions.question: His eldest sister is instrumental ______ his success.
questions.explanation: The fixed preposition is “instrumental to”.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The interpreter was wrong because he gave the congregation a ______ translation of the pastor’s statement.
questions.explanation: A word-for-word rendering is a literal translation.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which option has a different vowel sound from the others?
questions.explanation: foal /əʊ/, foe /əʊ/, mow /əʊ/; fowl /aʊ/ has a different diphthong.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: beige – same consonant sound as the underlined letter(s)
questions.explanation: The “ge” in beige is /ʒ/ (as in genre, measure, vision).

questions.subject: English
questions.question: renege – same consonant sound as the underlined letter(s)
questions.explanation: The “g” in renege is /g/ (hard g), same as in revenge.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: house – same consonant sound as the underlined letter(s)
questions.explanation: The “h” in house is pronounced /h/; who also begins with /h/. Honour, honest and hauteur have silent “h”.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the derivative of $f(x) = x^3 - 4x + 7$ with respect to $x$?
questions.explanation: Applying the power rule gives $3x^2 - 4 + 0 = 3x^2 - 4$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the sum of the interior angles of a convex polygon with $n$ sides?
questions.explanation: The formula for the sum of interior angles in an $n$-gon is $(n-2) \times 180^\circ$.

questions.explanation: Subtract 5 from both sides ($2x = 10$), then divide by 2 ($x = 5$).

questions.question: What is the value of $\sin(\frac{\pi}{6})$?
questions.explanation: $\sin(30^\circ) = \sin(\frac{\pi}{6}) = \frac{1}{2}$.
